Every run has holes in it. The trick is knowing exactly which ones before you're flipping through the back-issue bins.

Start a run on ComixCatalog and it keeps count for you: how many you own, the exact issues you're missing, and one button that puts every one of them on your wantlist. Already own a stack of a run? Mark it all at once, or select a range. Then print a checklist with yours already checked off. All free.

For the record, as of Oct 27: on League of Comic Geeks, the Missing Issues smart list is a Patron beta at $49 a year, and progress tracking is part of Pro.

The first 100 members are Founding Collectors: a numbered badge nobody after No. 100 can get, your name on the founders wall, and a lifetime membership. Link in bio.

The worst part of tracking your comics is the first 400 of them. Nobody wants to spend a weekend typing in a long box.

So don't. On ComixCatalog you scan a cover with your phone, or a whole stack and add them all at once. Own a full run? Mark it in one go. Already tracking on CLZ or League of Comic Geeks? Export your file and drop it in, and your grades, slabs and cert numbers come with it. All free.

The first 100 members are Founding Collectors: a numbered badge nobody after No. 100 can get, your name on the founders wall, and a lifetime membership. Link in bio.

If a pipe bursts over your long boxes, the hard part of the insurance claim isn't the forms. It's remembering exactly what you had.

On ComixCatalog, one button turns your collection into a dated PDF: covers, grade, slab and cert number, what you paid and an estimated value for each book. Print it, email it to your agent, keep a copy somewhere that isn't the basement. Free for every member.

The values are estimates from current listings and cover prices, so it's a record of what you own, not a formal appraisal.
